la:noun:fabula.html:
fābŭla, ae, f.
fari
,
a narration, narrative, account, story; the subject of common talk.
In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: narratio, fasti, annales, res gestae, historia): additur fabulae, quo vulgo Sabini aureas armillas brachio laevo habuerint, pepigisse eam, etc.,: poëticae (opp. incorrupta rerum gestarum monumenta), id. praef. § 6: Ummidius, qui tam (non longa est fabula) dives, ut, etc.,; : mutato nomine de te fabula narratur,: asinaeque paternum Cognomen vertas in risum et fabula flas,the common talk, town's talk,; cf.: heu me, per urbem Fabula quanta fui!: fabula (nec sentis) tota jactaris in urbe,you are talked of all over the city,; cf. ; ; : habes omnes fabulas urbis,: nova fabula,the news,: semper formosis fabula poena fuit, (3, 30, 26 M.): a diverticulo repetatur fabula,let us return to our story,.—
Transf., conversation (post-Aug.): ut fabulas quoque eorum et disputationes et arcana semotae dictionis penitus exciperem,conversations,: praeceptores cum auditoribus suis fabulas habent,; cf.: cum inter fabulas privatas sermo esset ortus, quanti, etc.,in private conversation,.—With a dependent clause: ne id accidat, quod cuipiam Thraco venisse usu, fabula est,is related,.—
In vulg. lang. (like the Germ. Geschichte), affair, concern, matter: sed quid ego aspicio? quae haec fabula'st?what sort of an affair is this?; .
In partic. (freq. and class.), a fictitious narrative, a tale, story (syn.: apologus, narratio): narrationum tris accepimus species, fabulam, quae versatur in tragoediis atque carminibus non a veritate modo, sed etiam a forma veritatis remota, argumentum ... historiam, etc., : haec res agetur nobis, vobis fabula,: peregrino narrare fabulas,: num igitur me cogis etiam fabulis credere? quae delectationis habeant quantum voles ... auctoritatem quidem nullam debemus nec fidem commenticiis rebus adjungere, etc.,; cf.: fictis fabulis,: antiquitas recepit fabulas, fictas etiam nonnumquam incondite,; cf.: a fabulis ad facta venire,fin.: minor fabulis habetur fides,: saepe fabulis fidem firmare (consuerant),; Liv. praef. § 6: non fabula rumor Ille fuit,: fabulam inceptat,: quid tamen ista velit sibi fabula, ede,: fabulae!mere stories! stuff! nonsense!; : ne convivialium fabularum simplicitas in crimen duceretur,: sufficiunt duae fabulae, an tertiam poscis?.—In apposition: jam te premet nox fabulaeque Manes (= fabulosi, inanes),: civis et manes et fabula fies,: nos jam fabula sumus,.—So of idle tales: ineptas et aniles fabulas devita, al.—
Of particular kinds of poetry.
Most freq., a dramatic poem, drama, play (syn.: ludus, cantus, actio, etc.): in full, fabula scaenica,; or, theatralis,: fabula ad actum scenarum composita,; cf. : Livianae fabulae non satis dignae, quae iterum legantur. Atque hic Livius primus fabulam, C. Clodio Caeci filio et M. Tuditano Cos. docuit,produced,; v. doceo, II. init.; cf.: fabulam dare, under do, II. H.; so, facere,: neque histrioni ut placeat, peragenda fabula est,: securus, cadat an recto stet fabula talo,: neve minor neu sit quinto productior actu Fabula,: M. Pacuvii nova fabula,: Terentii,: Attae, et saep.: in fabulis stultissima persona, et saep.— Transf.: non solum unum actum, sed totam fabulam confecissem,.—
A fable (cf. apologus): fabularum cur sit inventum genus Brevi docebo, etc.,: quae (res) vel apologum, vel fabulam vel aliquam contineat irrisionem,: nota illa de membris humanis adversus ventrem discordantibus fabula, (shortly before, fabella) et saep.—Prov.: Lupus in fabula (like the Engl., talk of the devil, and he will appear), of a person who comes just as we are talking about him, ; ; so, lupus in sermone,.

senses: to build, construct, fashion, forge, shape
la:verb:fabricor.html:
fā^brĭcor, ātus, 1 (archaic
inf. fabricarier, Poëta ap. ), v. dep. a., and (poet. and in post-Aug. prose) făbrĭ-co, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
fabrica
, to make out of wood, stone, metal, etc., to frame, forge, construct, build.
Lit.
Form fabricor: heu Mulciber, arma ignavo es invictā fabricatus manu, Att. ap. (R): ii, qui signa fabricantur,: Capitolii fastigium,: gladium, id. Rab. Post, 3, 7: Jovi fulmen,: naves,: pontes et scalas fabricati,: (mundum) globosum est fabricatus, Orell. N. cr. et saep.—
Form fabrico: hunc (cratera) fabricaverat Alcon,; cf.: pugnabant armis, quae post fabricaverat usus,: ratem,: fabricavit deceris Liburnicas,: vasa fabricabis,; —In pass.: fabricata fago pocula,carved, made,; cf.: simulacra ex auro vel argento fabricata,cast, molten,: in amphitheatro ligneo intra anni spatium fabricato,built,: tela reponuntur manibus fabricata Cyclopum,forged,; cf. ; ; : in nostros fabricata est machina muros,: di qui hominis manu fabricati sunt, et saep.—
Transf., in gen., to prepare, form, fashion.
Form fabricor: hoc affirmare potes, Luculle, esse aliquam vim cum prudentia et consilio scilicet, quae finxerit, vel, ut tuo verbo utar, quae fabricata sit hominem?; cf.: quanto quasi artificio natura fabricata esset primum animal omne, deinde hominem maxime,: opus est fabricanda ad fulmina nubi, Lachm. N. cr.; imitated: fabricantes fulmina nubes,: ut ea ipsa dii immortales ad usum hominum fabricati paene videantur,; cf. : prandium opipare,: quod nihil esset clarius ἐναργεία, ut Graeci: (perspicuitatem aut evidentiam nos, si placet, nominemus fabricemurque, si opus erit, verba), etc.,: fabricare quidvis, quidvis comminiscere,; cf.: compara, fabricare, finge quod lubet,. —Absol.: age modo, fabricamini,.—
Form fabrico: philosophia animum format et fabricat,: qui fabricaverat illum (Platonem),: ne fabricate moras,.—In pass.: dum illa verba fabricentur et memoriae insidant,.

la:noun:fabricator.html:
fā^brĭcātor, ōris, m.
id.
,
an artificer, framer, forger, contriver, fabricator (rare but class.).
Lit.: ille fabricator tanti operis (mundi),; so, mundi, Quint, 2, 16, 12; : minutorum opusculorum,: ipse doli (i. e. equi lignei) fabricator Epeos,: deorum, i. e. of statues of the gods, Firm. Math. 3, 6, 9.—
Trop.: dolor ac morbus leti fabricator uterque est,causer, producer,.

senses: of or pertaining to the gens Fabia.
la:adj:Fabius.html:
Făbĭus, a,
the name of a Roman gens, concerning which see -50; among its distinguished members were,
Fabius Pictor, a historian, .—
Q. Fabius Maximus Cunctator, the famous dictator in the second Punic war, ; passim.—
M. Fabius Quintilianus, author of the rhetorical work Institutiones Oratoriae, ; . —
Paulus Fabius Persicus, consul under Tiberius, A.U.C. 786, ; .—
Hence,
Făbĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Fabius, Fabian: lex, de ambitu and de plagiariis,; ; ; : fornix, a triumphal arch, built by Q. Fabius Maximus Allobrogicus on the Sacra Via, in the neighborhood of the Regia, ; called also Fornix Fabii,; and Fornix Fabianus, v. under B.: lupercus, cf. under B.: tribus,one of the rural tribes,.—
Făbĭānus, a, um, adj., the same: fornix, i. q. Fabius fornix (v. above),; also called arcus,: Fabianae artes,i. e. delay,: † Fabiani et † Quintilian appellabantur luperci, a Fabio et Quintilio praepositis suis, Paul. ex Müll. —Subst.: Făbĭāni, ōrum, m., persons of the Fabian tribe, ; also the soldiers of Fabius, .

la:adj:fabrilis.html:
fā^brīlis, e, adj.
faber
,
of or belonging to an artificer (class.): scalprum,: opera ad fabrilia surgere,: dextra,: vincula,: gluten,; cf. glutinum,: fumus gratiam affert vinis,; hence, uva,i. e. smoke-dried,: opera,: erratum, of the sculptor or artist, * .—In the neutr. subst.: fabrīlĭa, ium, mechanical tools or implements: tractant fabrilia fabri,.—* Adv.: fā^brīlĭter, skilfully, in a workmanlike manner: opifex fabriliter aptans Composuit,.

la:verb:fabulor.html:
fābŭlor, ātus (archaic
inf. praes. fabularier, ; ; ; ; ; also act. form fabulaverit, Afran. ap. dub.: fabulabere, R: fabulem, Fleck.), 1, v. dep. a. [fabula], to speak, converse, talk, chat (mostly ante- and post-class.; esp.

freq. in Plaut.; not in Cic.; syn.: aio, inquam, dico, loquor, etc.).

In gen.: ut pro viribus tacere ac fabulari tute noveris, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 182 ed. Vahl.): clare advorsum fabulabor,: reliqua alia,: ut aperte tibi nunc fabuler,: quod omnes homines fabulantur per vias, Mihi esse filiam inventam,: aliquid,to say, utter,: (ars medendi) ictum fulmine Aesculapium fabulata,: inter sese,: cum aliquo,; : stabant Fronto et Festus fabulantes,: inter fabulandum,.—
Esp., to speak a language: qui Obsce et Volsce fabulantur, Rib.

la:noun:fabrica.html:
fā^brĭca, ae, f.
1. faber
,
the workshop of an artisan who works in hard materials (syn.: taberna, officina).
Prop., ; : Vulcanus, qui Lemni fabricae traditur praefuisse,: armorum,armory, (for which: armorum officinae,).—
Transf., the art, trade, or profession of such an artisan, : pictura et fabrica ceteraeque artes habent quendam absoluti operis effectum,architecture,; cf. ; and: natura effectum esse mundum: nihil opus fuisse fabrica,: omnis fabrica aeris et ferri,: aeraria, ferrea, materiaria, the art of working in brass, etc., ; cf.: aerariae artis,; and: ejus fabricae, quam Graeci χαλκευτικὴν vocant, .—In apposition with ars: abies Graeco fabricae artis genere spectabilis,: servus arte fabrica peritus,: fanum solerti fabrica structum,with artistic skill,.—
In gen., any skilful production, a fabric, building, etc.: admirabilis membrorum animantium,

; cf. ; ; —Of man as the creature of God, . —

In the comic writers, a crafty device, trick, stratagem: ei nos facetis fabricis et doctis dolis Glaucumam ob oculos obiciemus,; : nescio quam fabricam facit,; : ad senem fingere,

fabula, II.

la:noun:faba.html:
făba, ae, f.
for fag-va, Sanscr. root bhaj-, to divide, share; bhak-tam, food; Gr. φαγ-εῖν, to eat; cf. fāgus
,
a bean, Vicia faba, Linn.; Gr. κύαμος, more correctly, perh., our horse-bean.
Prop., ; ; ; ; ; : perque fabam repunt (grues) et mollia crura reponunt, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 545 ed. Vahl.); not eaten by the Pythagoreans,; ; ; ; and neither to be touched nor named by the Flamen Dialis, Fab. Pict. ap. ; Paul. ex Müll.—
Prov.
St. Repperi. Ly. Quid repperisti? St. Non quod pueri clamitant, In faba se repperisse, .—
Istaec in me cudetur faba, i. e. I shall have to smart for it, Don.—
Tam perit quam extrema faba, in proverbio est, quod ea plerumque aut proteritur aut decerpitur a praetereuntibus, Fest. S. V. TAM, p. 363, 17 Müll.—
Transf., of things of a similar shape: of grains of wheat, : faba caprini fimi,goat's dung,.—As a measure, .
